Matrix transforms

OFFLINE PRACTICE · No account, AI request, or network required. Answers are included for study. This is not an official grade.

Learn one step at a time

Start from coordinates

Represent the point (1,0) as the homogeneous column vector (1,0,1)^T. This lets a 3x3 affine matrix express translation as well as scale and rotation.

Evidence / 依据: AB-S1

Apply one matrix at a time

For this lesson only, apply S then R then T, giving p'=T R S p. The rightmost matrix acts first on a column vector; there is no universal default order.

Evidence / 依据: AB-S1

Compare the result

Scale (1,0) by 2 to (2,0), rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise to (0,2), then add (1,1) to get (1,3). Reversing the operations gives (-2,4). Results can differ, though some special transformations commute.

Sources and permissions

AB-S1 · Original synthetic transform note

This example uses homogeneous column vectors p=(x,y,1)^T. We choose scale S, then rotation R, then translation T, so p'=T R S p. This is an explicit example order, not a universal default. Affine translation uses homogeneous coordinates. For p=(1,0), scale uniformly by 2, rotate 90 degrees counterclockwise, then translate by (1,1): (1,0) -> (2,0) -> (0,2) -> (1,3). Reversing those operations gives (-2,4), not (1,3). Some special transforms commute; order does not always change the result.
